thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 router egress latency spike in us-west-2 detected. p99 ~ 3.2s over last 5m, streaming stalls observed. Paging eng-sre and runtime.

alex: oncall here, looking now. any customer impact flags?

jamie: seeing a bunch of small traces blaming misroute -> requests being sent to a small set of shards (hot partition). probably policy-weight drift after the rollout at 02:17.

maria: +1. Telemetry shows routing policy committed (commit abc123) pushed a zone-preference change. weight for zone-usw2 jumped to 0.92 for model-slicing. That created a hot partition on backend shard 14.

sam: customer-impact: support reports 3 streaming customers with stalls (session reconnects), ~120k tokens affected in last 10m. billing not impacted but UX degraded.

beth: listing affected tenants we pulled from support dashboard: tenant-phi, tenant-hub, tenant-trace. Customer-facing notes queued, no public report yet.

jamie: diagnostic quick dump:
```
# top hot backend shards
curl -s http://router-metrics.usw2.internal/hot_shards | jq . | head
{
  "shard_14": {"qps": 420, "latency_p99_ms": 3200},
  "shard_73": {"qps": 50, "latency_p99_ms": 200},
}
```

maria: I see KV cache eviction rate spike on shard_14, likely because too many heads routed there. Also observed streaming incomplete frames and RSTs from proxy.

alex: can we mitigate without full rollback? options: 1) quick rollback of the policy commit, 2) apply temporary ejection of shard_14, 3) lower zone-usw2 weight to fallback and redistribute. Which is fastest?

jamie: fastest is reduce zone weight to 0.5 and enable eager fallback. rollback touches rollout system and might take longer due to canary window. Ejection needs ops approval.

ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-hotshard (recommended: reduce weight -> monitor 5m -> rollback if not recovered)

maria: I'll push a manual override to routing control plane to lower zone weight. Doing a dry-run first.

alex: go for it, please post commands.

maria: executing:
```bash
# temp override
redwoodctl routing override set --policy model-slicing --zone usw2 --weight 0.5 --reason "hotshard mitigation"
redwoodctl routing reload --policy model-slicing --sync
```

maria: override applied. new target weight 0.5. pushing to 3 control-plane nodes.

jamie: seeing immediate traffic shift. shard_14 qps dropping from 420 -> 110 in last 30s. p99 trending down.

beth: customers on streaming sessions reporting partial recovery for some connections. still seeing intermittent stalls.

sam: what's the fallback policy? do we have model-variant fallback to cpu/gpu-slow?

maria: fallback already enabled: requests redirected to compatible variant in euw1 if local hotspot, but that adds cross-region latency. Not great but better than stalls.

jamie: oncall note: keep metrics window open for 20m. If p99 > 1.5s after 10m, prepare rollback of commit abc123.

incident-bot: Update: mitigation override applied by maria. Incident severity escalated to Sev2. Live bridge scheduled if > 10 customers impacted.

alex: I'm going to hand off to jamie for live monitoring; I'm taking support coordination with beth.

jamie: ack, I'll watch routing heatmaps and tail latency. Starting a short trace capture for hotspot shard_14 (5m).

(10m later)
jamie: metrics update: p95 -> 420ms (was 700ms), p99 -> 950ms (was 3.2s). streaming RSTs down 78%. good progress.
maria: cache warm-up is happening on new shards, prefix hits increasing. K/V cache hit-rate for model X rose 18% since override.

beth: support update: pushed interim message to affected customers, invited them to opt into cross-region fallback, three accepted.
sam: are there any related rollouts in the last 24h we should pin for RCA?
jamie: yes, rollout abc123 (zone preference tuning) at 02:17 and a minor placement tweak at 05:03. I'll collect diffs.

alex: do we want to keep override or roll back the rollout? pros/cons?
maria: override buys time and gives smoother redistribution; rollback removes the policy change entirely, good for RCA but will force a new rollout. I'd keep override for now until we validate telemetry for 1 hour.

jamie: agreed. schedule: keep override for 1h, continue monitoring, prepare rollback playbook if we see regression.

incident-bot: Incident timeline appended to ticket INC-2026-321. Please add postmortem notes when available.

beth: support log attached to INC-2026-321: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-2026-321/attachments/streaming-logs.txt

alex: handing off active monitoring to jamie. If metrics regress, page me and jump to live bridge. Closing my shift in 30m.
jamie: acknowledged. I'll ping oncall-bridge if any customer-impact spike.

(End of thread)
